title: Siam & Ratchaprasong 2026 — Bangkok's Mega-Mall District Guide | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Guide to Siam & Ratchaprasong, central Bangkok's shopping core. Walk the covered Skywalk mall-to-mall without touching the street, pay respects at the Erawan Shrine, and learn which mall sells what, where to eat, and which BTS station to use.
keywords: Siam Ratchaprasong, Siam malls Bangkok, Ratchaprasong Skywalk, Erawan Shrine, Bangkok shopping district
intro: Siam and Ratchaprasong make up central Bangkok's shopping core, and you can reach all of it on foot via the Skywalk — an elevated walkway that takes you from BTS Siam all the way to Chit Lom without ever stepping down into the sun and traffic. Along the way you'll find luxury malls, teen-fashion malls, food halls, and the Erawan Shrine packed with worshippers every single day. This is a district you can wander all day with barely any planning.
chips: 🚇 Get off at BTS Siam/Chit Lom

blocks.html: If there's one district in Bangkok that sums up the phrase "city center," it's Siam running into Ratchaprasong. This stretch has malls lined up one after another — Siam Paragon, Siam Center, Siam Discovery, then across to CentralWorld, Gaysorn Village, all the way to Central Chidlom and Central Embassy. You can reach every one of them on the Skywalk without ever touching the street or hailing a ride.

What's great about this district is that it works for every budget and every style. Come to browse luxury labels, shop for teen fashion, grab a meal in a food court, or just pay respects at a shrine and stroll around taking photos — it all fits. We'll walk you through what each spot is like, where to start, and when the crowds are thick or thin.

blocks.text: Where to start: which BTS station?

blocks.html: The easiest and most reliable way to get here is the BTS, because the district straddles two stations perfectly. For the Siam-side malls, get off at BTS Siam (the interchange where the Sukhumvit and Silom lines cross), step out the gate and walk straight into Siam Paragon or Siam Center. For the CentralWorld–Ratchaprasong–Gaysorn side, BTS Chit Lom is closer.

items: BTS Siam — close to Siam Paragon, Siam Center, Siam Discovery, Siam Square
BTS Chit Lom — close to CentralWorld, Gaysorn Village, Central Chidlom, Big C Ratchadamri
Between the two stations — the Skywalk connects them the whole way, passing right in front of CentralWorld and the Ratchaprasong intersection

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: On weekends and in the early evening, the Skywalk in front of CentralWorld gets very crowded — walk slowly and keep an eye on your bag. If you want an easy stroll, come before noon when the malls have just opened (most open at 10am) and it's still quiet.

blocks.text: The Skywalk — the artery of this district

blocks.html: The Skywalk is an elevated walkway running beneath the BTS track, linking everything from Siam station past the front of CentralWorld all the way to Chit Lom station. The CentralWorld–Ratchaprasong section is a wide, covered walkway several hundred meters long — easy to walk and sheltered from sun and rain. That's why so many people can spend the whole day in this district without ever really hitting the street.

A favorite photo spot is the middle of the Skywalk at the Ratchaprasong intersection, where mall signs light up in every direction — especially pretty at night. On the Ratchadamri side there's a separate elevated walkway (R Walk) branching off toward Big C Ratchadamri, The Market, and Gaysorn Village.
The malls here have distinctly different personalities — knowing them in advance lets you head straight for the right spot and not waste time.

items.name: Siam Paragon
items.blurb: The biggest mall on the Siam side, spanning luxury labels to everyday brands. Has a car showroom, the Gourmet Eats food hall on floor G, and SEA LIFE (the aquarium) on the lower level. Built for a long, slow wander.

items.name: Siam Center + Siam Discovery
items.blurb: Bold design, packed with Thai designer labels and homeware. Connects directly to Paragon. Best for fashion lovers and craft hunters.

items.name: Siam Square
items.blurb: Across from Paragon, an open-air teen district full of clothing shops, cafes, and wallet-friendly snack spots. The Siam Square One plaza often hosts events.

items.name: CentralWorld
items.blurb: The biggest mall on the Ratchaprasong side, with a huge number of stores and the Groove dining zone. The plaza out front is a major venue for events and the New Year countdown.

items.name: Gaysorn Village + Gaysorn Amarin
items.blurb: The luxury-label and premium-dining side, quieter than the other malls. Connects from the Skywalk.

items.name: Central Chidlom + Central Embassy
items.blurb: On the Phloen Chit side. Central Chidlom is Central's flagship store, while Embassy gathers high-fashion brands and the Eathai food hall on the basement level.

blocks.title: How to walk it without getting lost
blocks.html: Every mall connects to the Skywalk mainly through floor 1 or floor M. If you can't find the link, head up to the floor that lines up with the BTS exit, look for the Skywalk sign, and just follow it — no need to go down to the street below.

blocks.text: Erawan Shrine — the spiritual heart of the district

blocks.html: Right at the Ratchaprasong intersection, on the corner in front of the Grand Hyatt Erawan, stands the Erawan Shrine (Thao Maha Phrom) — a four-faced Brahma shrine where Thais and foreign visitors crowd in to pay respects every day. It's free to enter and open roughly 6am–6pm, with no admission fee. You can reach it from both BTS Chit Lom and Siam, with the Skywalk bringing you right down to it.

The traditional way to pay respects is to start at the first face and move clockwise around all four. Offering sets are sold at stalls around the shrine — usually 12 incense sticks, 4 candles, a garland, and gold leaf — starting at just a few tens of baht. If a wish has been granted, there's also a traditional dance service to give thanks (roughly 8am–5pm).

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The shrine sits in the middle of a busy, crowded intersection. Weekday evenings and weekends are packed. If you want a calm atmosphere and good photos, come in the morning around 7–9am — fewer people and nicer light.

blocks.text: Not just one shrine — the Ratchaprasong cluster of deities

blocks.html: Many people don't realize there are several Hindu shrines scattered around the Ratchaprasong intersection, close enough to visit one after another in a single trip. Those into spiritual merit-making like to hit them all.

items: Erawan Shrine — in front of the Grand Hyatt Erawan on the corner of the Ratchaprasong intersection. You can pray for anything; it's the best-known of the lot.
Trimurti + Ganesha — the plaza in front of CentralWorld on the former Isetan side. People come to pray for love (Trimurti) and career success (Ganesha), traditionally on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
Indra on Erawan the elephant — at the corner of Amarin / Gaysorn Amarin, for victory and authority.
Lakshmi and Narayana — around Gaysorn Village, for wealth and good fortune.

blocks.text: Where to eat in this district

blocks.html: You'll never go hungry here. Every mall has its own dining zone, from light-on-the-wallet food courts to comfortable sit-down restaurants. We've picked the spots people go to most and that are easy to find.

items.name: Gourmet Eats, Siam Paragon
items.blurb: Paragon's floor-G food hall, gathering famous street-food vendors and dessert shops in one place. Styled like an old-town quarter and run on a card system. Great for lunch when it's busy.
items.meta: Floor G, Siam Paragon · open with the mall, ~10am–10pm

items.name: Eathai, Central Embassy
items.blurb: Embassy's basement-level Thai food hall, bringing together dishes from every region of Thailand plus souvenirs. Nice atmosphere — ideal for showing foreign visitors the full spread of Thai food.
items.meta: Floor LG, Central Embassy · Phloen Chit side

items.name: Groove, CentralWorld
items.blurb: An open-air dining zone in front of CentralWorld, mixing cafes and restaurants with a relaxed, sit-and-chill vibe — both Thai and international. Good for meeting friends in the evening.

items.name: Gourmet Market, Paragon
items.blurb: A premium supermarket on floor G next to the food hall, with ready-to-eat meals and snacks you can pack back to the hotel. Great for imported souvenirs and treats.

items.name: Snack spots at Siam Square
items.blurb: The Siam Square side is packed with bubble-tea shops, fried snacks, and teen desserts at easy prices. Graze as you go — perfect for a snack break between malls.

blocks.text: How to make the most of a single day

blocks.html: If you've only got one day and want to cover the whole district, try pacing it like this — walking along the Skywalk from one end to the other without backtracking.

items.activity: Get off at BTS Siam and walk into Siam Paragon
items.note: The mall has just opened — still quiet and easy to walk
They connect directly; check out the design labels and homeware

items.activity: Lunch at Gourmet Eats on floor G, Paragon
items.note: Street food all in one place; go before noon for fewer crowds
Covered the whole way, no sun — stop for photos at the Ratchaprasong intersection

items.activity: Pay respects at Trimurti–Ganesha in front of CentralWorld
items.note: The plaza on the former Isetan side

items.activity: Visit the Erawan Shrine at the corner of the Ratchaprasong intersection
items.note: Buy an offering set at the stalls beside the shrine, then circle all four faces clockwise

blocks.title: Wrap up on the Chit Lom–Phloen Chit side

items.activity: Walk on to Gaysorn Village or Central Chidlom

items.note: Thai food from every region in the basement food hall

blocks.text: Things to know before you go

items: Most malls open ~10am–10pm. If you come earlier, you can only walk the Skywalk and visit the shrines.
Avoid the traffic — the Ratchaprasong intersection jams up badly in the evening, so the BTS is by far your best bet. Don't try to take a taxi into this district at the end of the workday.
Mind your belongings in the crowds — the Skywalk and the area around the shrine get packed, so wear your bag in front.
Dress modestly at the shrines — you don't need to cover up completely, but skip anything too revealing out of respect.
Clean restrooms in every mall, free to use, so that's one thing you won't have to worry about all day.

faq.q: Which BTS station should I use for Siam–Ratchaprasong?
faq.a: If you're walking the Siam-side malls (Paragon, Siam Center, Siam Discovery), get off at BTS Siam. But for CentralWorld, Ratchaprasong, Gaysorn, or the Erawan Shrine, BTS Chit Lom is closer. Both stations connect along the Skywalk the whole way, so you never have to touch the street.

faq.q: What are the Erawan Shrine's hours, and is there an entry fee?
faq.a: It's open for prayers every day, roughly 6am–6pm, with no admission fee. Offering sets are sold at stalls around the shrine, starting at just a few tens of baht. If you want a calm atmosphere and fewer people, come in the morning around 7–9am.

faq.q: Is it far to walk from Siam to CentralWorld?
faq.a: Not far. Walking the Skywalk from BTS Siam to the front of CentralWorld takes about 5–10 minutes, and it's covered the whole way — no sun, no rain, and no crossing the street below.

faq.q: What budget does this district suit?
faq.a: It works for any budget — from grazing on cheap snacks at Siam Square to shopping luxury labels at Gaysorn or Embassy. On a tight budget you can easily fill a whole day walking the Skywalk, visiting the shrines, and eating in the food courts without spending much.

faq.q: How many shrines are there to visit around Ratchaprasong?
faq.a: There are several you can visit one after another. The best-known is the Erawan Shrine in front of the Grand Hyatt. Beyond that there's the Trimurti and Ganesha in front of CentralWorld, Indra on the Erawan elephant, and Lakshmi near Gaysorn Village. Spiritual visitors like to hit them all in one trip.
